name: Tripoli
subtitle: Tripoli, capital of Libya: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 1,063,571 people live in the Tripoli District (counted 2006).
Tripoli was founded in the 7th century BC as the Phoenician settlement of Oea, forming with Sabratha and Leptis Magna the historic Tripolis.
The marble Arch of Marcus Aurelius, erected in 163–165 AD, stands in the Medina as the sole surviving monument of Roman Oea.

parts.text: Tripoli was founded in the 7th century BC by Phoenician traders under the name Oea, one of the three coastal colonies of Tripolitania.
Conquered by Ottoman forces in 1551, Tripoli developed into an autonomous maritime power under the Karamanli dynasty in the 18th and early 19th centuries.
Upon the declaration of Libyan independence in 1951, Tripoli was established as national co-capital with Benghazi before becoming the sole permanent capital.

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in the Tripoli District?

parts.text: 1,063,571 in the 2006 census recorded by the Bureau of Statistics and Census of Libya. Subsequent estimates suggest an urban population of 1.2 to 1.3 million, though no formal nationwide census has been completed since 2006.

items.text: Phoenicians establish the coastal trading colony of Oea.
The marble Arch of Marcus Aurelius is erected in Roman Oea.
Ahmad Karamanli founds the autonomous Karamanli dynasty ruling Tripoli.
Mustafa Gurgi completes the 16-domed Gurgi Mosque in the Medina.
Libyan independence is proclaimed under King Idris I; Tripoli becomes co-capital.
